# dsh-memory-vault
**Local-first long-term memory and personal-profile plugin for DeepSeek Harness.**
Distill SOPs, best practices, and personal preferences in any session; recall them automatically in
new conversations; aggregate everything into a personal profile by life domain. All data stays in a
local SQLite file — zero external services, zero runtime dependencies, clean uninstall.
中文文档 · Design · Dev journal · GUI verification
## 1. What problem it solves
Harness conversations are "one-shot": switch sessions, wait a few days, and the AI forgets who you a
re, what your project conventions are, and which pitfalls you already hit.
| Pain point | Solution here |
| Amnesia across sessions | **Automatic recall** before every first step: hybrid-ranked memories inj

ected under a hard budget |
| Distillation is left to the AI's mood | Explicit "remember this" write
s land directly; AI-extracted candidates go to a **confirmation queue** — nothing becomes active wit

hout your approval |
| Memories are flat sentences | Seven structured kinds (preference / fact / dec

ision / constraint / lesson / sop / event / summary); SOPs carry ordered steps |
| Domains all mixed
together | First-class **domain dimension** (dev / career / workflow / english / investment, editab

le) |
| Store but never use | **Personal profile analysis**: per-domain aggregation of preferences,

SOP inventory, lessons, decisions + optional LLM narrative |
| Opaque data | One-click human-readabl
e Markdown export; JSONL backup/restore; every memory traceable to its source turn |

## 3. Features in detail
### 3.1 Structured memory model
Every memory carries these dimensions (`mvault_add` parameters):
| Dimension | Values | Notes |
| `kind` | `preference` / `fact` / `decision` / `constraint` / `lesson` / `sop` / `event` / `summary

` | **sop + steps = ordered workflow** |
| `track` | `user` / `global` / `project` / `project-log` /

`daily-log` | Layered tracks (3.2) |
| `domain` | `dev` / `career` / `workflow` / `english` / `inve

stment` / `general` (editable) | Used for recall weighting, filtering, profile aggregation |
| `impo

rtance` / `confidence` | 0–1 | Ranking and extraction thresholds |
| `stableKey` | any stable id | U

pdating the same fact **supersedes** the old value; old version kept, reversible |
| `steps` | strin

g array | Ordered SOP steps |
| `branches` | git branch names | Branch scoping for project memories

(3.4) |
| `tags` | short labels | Retrieval helpers |
| `entities` / `relations` | entities and dire
cted edges | Woven into the knowledge graph (3.6) |
### 3.2 Five memory tracks
| Track | What goes in | Recall behavior |

| `user` | Your preferences, habits, communication style | Recalled + profiled |
| `global` | Cross-

project facts, SOPs, lessons | Recalled + profiled |
| `project` | Project key facts (decisions, con

ventions, pitfalls) | Recalled; **filtered by git branch scope** |
| `project-log` | Project progres

s stream | Never auto-injected; on-demand reads + export |
| `daily-log` | Daily progress stream | N
ever auto-injected; on-demand reads + export |
### 3.3 Three write gates (who writes, how it takes effect)
| Gate | Trigger | Destination | Rationale |
| ① Explicit | You say "记住…" → `mvault_add` | **Active immediately** | User-intent, zero trust cost

|
| ② Extraction | Completed turn → background LLM distillation (`autoExtract: true`) | **Confirmati

on queue** — active only after approval | The AI proposes, you decide |
| ③ Progress logs | `mvault_
add` to `project-log`/`daily-log` | Active but **excluded from auto-recall** | Traceability without
`project-log`/`daily-log` | Active but **excluded from auto-recall** | Traceability without noise |
> Difference from similar plugins: automatic extraction **never writes active memories directly**.
### 3.4 Automatic cross-session recall

- Hooks `agent/pre-step` (first step of every turn), on by default;
- Hybrid ranking = lexical FTS5
trigram (Chinese-friendly, incl. 2-char-term fallback) × graph distance × importance × half-life rec

ency (30d default) × access reinforcement × **domain weighting** (six configurable weights);

## 6. Data & security
- Database: `$DSH_HOME/dsh-memory-vault.sqlite`, `0600`, WAL mode; `application_id` rejects foreign

databases.
- Recall content is recorded in the session log (sessions stay reconstructable); injected

content is explicitly marked as reference data.
- Turn archives are bounded (100K chars / 30K token

s, 30 days); clipping is reported truthfully.
- Failed writes go to an outbox and replay at startup;

permanent failures land in a dead-letter file.
- Panel API is loopback/trusted-host only; mutations

require a process-random token; `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Data is 100% local. Enabling `autoExtr
act` or the narrative profile sends the relevant transcript/aggregate to your configured model route
ct` or the narrative profile sends the relevant transcript/aggregate to your configured model route.
## 7. Known limitations
- Single-writer model: one writable database per DSH process (SQLite WAL + busy_timeout cover normal

transactions; no distributed coordination).
- Recall is **lexical** (trigram overlap): cross-langua

ge semantic matching is not bundled (optional embeddings on the roadmap).
- Some Node versions log a

n experimental-API warning for `node:sqlite` (harmless).
- No built-in cross-device sync: use `mvaul

t_export` / `mvault_backup` + git.
- `autoExtract` needs a working model route; failures retry with
the archive preserved — no data loss, no turn blockage.
